json-to-xml.formula:
object  -> <key>...children...</key>
array   -> one <key> element per item (name repeats)
string/number/boolean -> <key>text</key>
null    -> <key/>
"@name" key -> attribute name="value"
"#text" key -> text content of the element
invalid chars in names -> replaced with _

keyFacts: JSON to XML converts any JSON document into well-formed XML entirely in your browser.
Objects become elements, arrays become repeated elements, null becomes a self-closing element.
Keys starting with @ become XML attributes; the #text key sets an element's text content.
Element names are sanitized (invalid characters become _) so output is always well-formed.
Special characters (&, <, >, ") are escaped in text and attribute values.
An optional XML declaration (<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>) heads the output.

limitations: JSON and XML model data differently, so conversion is a practical mapping - not a guaranteed round-trip.
Duplicate object keys keep only the last value, since JSON parsing resolves them silently.
Very deep documents may produce deeply nested XML that is hard to read.
Namespaces (xmlns) are not generated; add them manually if your target schema needs them.

json-to-xml.workedExample:
Input:
{"order": {"@id": "A1023", "customer": "Asha Sharma", "paid": true, "note": null}}

Output (root = "root"):
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<root>
  <order id="A1023">
    <customer>Asha Sharma</customer>
    <paid>true</paid>
    <note/>
  </order>
</root>

@id became the id attribute, "paid" became text, and null became the self-closing <note/>.
